chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Iblees says to his army, 'Cast envy and transgression between them, for both of these equate to Shirk in the presence of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: Why are envy and transgression considered equivalent to Shirk in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reveals the strategic priority of Satan, who instructs his legions to sow envy (*al-hasad*) and transgression (*al-bagh*) among humanity. This highlights a profound Shia theological insight: while Shirk is the ultimate sin, the subtle corruption of social bonds and individual excesses are deemed equally weighty in divine judgment, serving as effective precursors to major disbelief.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ibleesla is saying to hisla army, ‘Cast the envy and the transgression to be between them (the people), for both of these equate to the association (Shirk) in the Presence of Allahazwj’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Satan says to his soldiers, ‘Throw unto them envy and tyrannical transgression; in the sight of Allah these two are equal to considering things as partners of Allah.’”
